description: Synthetic fixed weather profiles used for repeatable commercial scenarios. Temperature values preserve the current model calibration; solar values preserve the current orientation irradiance profiles.

profiles.physical_rationale: Dry cold week for H1 zones: daily average close to 0 C, -4/+4 C oscillation to test heat losses and heating power.
profiles.client_description_fr: Reference cold weather for H1 zones, representative of a demanding winter week. It compares heating needs and comfort on a stable basis, identical for every file.
sources: Values preserved from scripts/create_customer_experience.py before Phase 5 externalization
RT2012 H1 climate zoning defined by the order of October 26, 2010, appendix I

profiles.physical_rationale: Temperate cold week for H2 zones: daily average at 3 C, keeping the same daily cycle as H1 to isolate the climate zone effect.
profiles.client_description_fr: Reference winter weather for H2 zones, with moderate but lasting cold. It quantifies heating savings on a scenario comparable across projects.
sources: Values preserved from scripts/create_customer_experience.py before Phase 5 externalization
RT2012 H2 climate zoning defined by the order of October 26, 2010, appendix I

profiles.physical_rationale: Mediterranean winter week for H3 zones: 7 C base, enough to test heating without overstating continental cold.
profiles.client_description_fr: Reference winter weather for H3 zones, suited to Mediterranean climates. It gives a cautious basis for estimating heating needs without using an extreme cold spell.
sources: Values preserved from scripts/create_customer_experience.py before Phase 5 externalization
RT2012 H3 climate zoning defined by the order of October 26, 2010, appendix I

profiles.physical_rationale: Common summer day for H1 zones: 22.5 C average, 5 C amplitude, useful for separating normal summer comfort from a heatwave episode.
profiles.client_description_fr: Typical summer weather for H1 zones. It shows expected comfort outside heatwaves and highlights the everyday effect of glazing, shutters, and inertia.
